disease_label_per_paper: Osmotic demyelination syndrome as the initial manifestation of a hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
presentation_summary: 47-year-old man arrived to the emergency room with generalized tonic-clonic seizures and altered mental status.
He had long-standing uncontrolled type 2 diabetes treated irregularly with insulin and metformin, HbA1c 10.1%, and 24 hours of nocturia, polyuria, and polydipsia.
Admission vitals were blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 85/min, respiratory rate 20/min, temperature 36.5 degC, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Exam showed remarkably dry mucous membranes, lethargy with Glasgow Coma Scale 11/15, lower-extremity strength 4/5, and diminished deep tendon reflexes.
Venous blood gas showed pH 7.36, PCO2 42 mmHg, lactate 1.2 mmol/L, and bicarbonate 23.7 mEq/L; urinary and plasma ketones were negative.
Laboratory values included glucose 838 mg/dL, BUN 21 mg/dL, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, sodium 133 mmol/L, chloride 89 mmol/L, serum albumin 2.1 g/dL, and serum osmolality 320 mOsm/kg.

outcome.source_text_value: During the next 3 weeks the patient progressively regained consciousness and muscle strength; at 6-month follow-up he was asymptomatic and MRI showed no residual damage.

quality_warnings: ODS MRI confirmation is preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking imaging; presentation ranking uses seizures and altered mental status rather than MRI confirmation.
Negative urinary and plasma ketones are rankable because they are part of the presentation laboratory state.
Anion gap 21 is retained from Table 1 even though pH and bicarbonate were not acidotic; this represents real HHS boundary evidence rather than a deletion target.
